title: Tool namespace gateway and telemetry bridge for OpenAI/legacy function interoperability
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers use two primary invocation styles: OpenAI-style 'tools' (name/description/json_schema) and Redwood legacy functions (RPC-like names and typed params). This causes name collisions, inconsistent telemetry, and complexity in streaming/structured outputs. We need a thin runtime gateway that normalizes call surfaces at the edge, maps naming/namespace collisions, and emits unified telemetry so backend routing, billing, and quality evals work consistently.

Goal: Implement a 'Tool Namespace Gateway' at the API ingress that: 1) resolves name collisions deterministically using a priority matrix (customer-owned namespaces > model-provided alias > legacy function registry), 2) normalizes parameter shapes and JSON schemas into a canonical intermediate form for the runtime, 3) preserves streaming semantics and partial outputs for functions/tools that stream responses, and 4) emits a telemetry 'bridge' record capturing both the original invocation metadata and the resolved canonical call for downstream observability, billing, and eval-ing.

Scope: runtime gateway + compatibility shim, mapping rules, telemetry schema, unit/integration tests, a small console UI to inspect resolution logs (read-only), rollout plan with canary, and docs for SDKs. Not in scope: changing model catalog UX or full rewrite of legacy function typing system.
comments: 2025-02-15 Priya Kapoor: Kickoff - defined success metrics: deterministic name resolution (>99.9% stable for same inputs), telemetry schema v1 adopted by console, zero-customer-facing behavior change for existing pinned mappings.

2025-02-18 Diego Morales: Implementation proposal posted. Key decision: do canonicalization at the edge (API gateway) rather than in downstream runtime to minimize downstream changes. Trade-offs discussed: small latency increase (~3-8ms) vs larger refactor risk if placed downstream.

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel (Design): Reviewed telemetry sample UI. Suggested adding a compact 'resolution trail' showing resolved_namespace -> resolver_reason -> fallbacks used. We'll include in console read-only view.

2025-02-24 QA notes (Marco Lin): Added unit tests for schema normalization and fuzz tests for name collisions. Found edge case when two tools differ only by punctuation; resolved by normalizing punctuation and whitespace in names.

2025-02-27 Diego Morales: First implementation branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/feature/tool-gateway. Draft PR created with gateway middleware, name-priority table, and telemetry event emitter. Needs security review for metadata logging (sensitive param redaction).

2025-03-01 Security (Lina Chen): Reviewed metadata logging. Approved with redaction rules: secrets and string values > 1024 chars are redacted; numeric/enum params are allowed. Updated telemetry schema v1.1.
2025-03-01 Priya Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria and added canary rollout plan to comments. Ready for engineering review and staging deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway resolves tool/function names according to priority matrix and returns resolved_name in API response metadata for all formats (JSON, streaming SSE).
Canonical parameter shape generated for both OpenAI-style tool schemas and legacy function signatures with documented mapping rules.
Streaming behavior preserved: partial tokens and structured 'tool_response' chunks are emitted during streaming and can be mapped back to original invocation names.

Telemetry bridge event published for every invocation with fields: original_name, resolved_name, resolver_reason, mapping_version, and redacted_params. Telemetry volume validated against staging sample.
No regressions on existing customer pinned mappings (regression test suite passes).
Console read-only view shows resolution trail for sampled requests and links back to raw logs.
steps: Design name-priority matrix and normalization rules (punctuation, whitespace, casing, aliases).
Implement gateway middleware that accepts both tool schema and legacy function payloads and outputs canonical call descriptor.
Add streaming-compatible encoder that inserts resolution metadata while preserving token-level streaming semantics.
Implement telemetry bridge emitter with redaction pipeline and versioned schema (v1.1).
Write unit and integration tests, including fuzzing for name collisions and long param payloads.
Create a staging canary: 1% traffic to gateway with logging enabled; run for 72 hours and validate metrics.
Ship console read-only inspector and docs for SDKs describing new metadata fields and migration guidance.
implementation_notes: Edge middleware will run in the API ingress tier written in Go. Use existing registry service for legacy function metadata; augment with 'alias' table for OpenAI-style tools. Resolver algorithm: 1) exact match (namespace-aware) 2) normalized match (strip punctuation/case) 3) alias lookup 4) fallback to legacy registry if permitted by customer policy. Emit telemetry as batched protobuf events to telemetry pipeline; include mapping_version header. Streaming: for SSE/HTTP chunked responses, inject a leading resolution control-chunk (non-customer-facing) before token stream to allow clients to associate partial outputs with resolved call. Ensure SDKs ignore control-chunk by version check. Add feature flag 'tool_gateway_v1' for controlled rollout. Maintain mapping_version to allow rollbacks.
